title: Tier Exception Approvals Decided on the Standard Timeframe (Formulary Benefit)
content:
## Clause

Under the Formulary Benefit, when a tier exception request decided on the standard timeframe is approved, the length of the approval is worked out from the member's records.

A tier exception approval's period is fixed only after every non-formulary exception request of the member that fell due earlier than the tier exception request carries a decision on record. For this ordering a request falls due at its latest supporting statement plus the formulary's decision hours for the request's priority.

Put in terms of the records: the period is settled once the member's exception history shows a decision on every non-formulary exception request whose due moment comes before the tier request's own. A request's due moment is the time of its latest supporting statement plus the decision hours for its priority, standard or expedited.

A tier exception approval is effective on the decision date and runs for its tier approval period, a whole number of calendar months. Its expiration date is the day before the same day-of-month that many months later. When that day does not exist, the last day of that month is used, and the expiration date is the day before it.

## Recording tool: `approve_tier_exception_8a527f11`

**Capability.** One call adds one approval decision to the tier exception request's case history, dated today, recorded as decided on the standard timeframe and covering the drug at the tier given. The approval is effective today and expires on the day before the same day-of-month the given number of whole months later (with the month-end rule above). The member's claims for the drug are covered at that tier through that date. The tool makes this single write. It checks nothing about eligibility, conditions or the values given.

**Invocation.** This is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks `approve_tier_exception_8a527f11` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `formulary_assignment_id` | reference number of the member's formulary assignment, as read from the formulary assignment lookup for the member | identifier |
| `source_exception_id` | reference number of the original exception request being approved, read from the member's exception history (the request row itself, not its statement row) | identifier |
| `drug_name` | the drug of the request | exactly one drug master list name: atorvastatin, lisinopril, metformin, sertraline, levothyroxine, sumatriptan, oxycodone-acetaminophen, insulin glargine-yfgn, Lantus, Eliquis, Xarelto, Jardiance, Ozempic, Mounjaro, Wegovy, Zepbound, Trelegy Ellipta, Breztri Aerosphere, Nurtec ODT, Ubrelvy, Humira, adalimumab-adaz, Dupixent, Skyrizi, Rinvoq, Enbrel, Biktarvy, Ibrance |
| `approved_tier` | the cost-share tier at which the approved exception covers the drug | enum: `1` (the generic tier), `2` (the preferred brand tier), `3` (the non-preferred brand tier), `4` (the first specialty tier), `5` (the second specialty tier), `not_applicable` (only for a record that carries no approval; never correct on an approval) |
| `approval_months` | the length of the approval in whole calendar months | whole number of months, no decimals |

A parameter's presence means only that the value is needed at call time.

**Return.** The receipt carries:
- `formulary_exception_id`, the reference number of the approval decision;
- `source_exception_id`, the request approved;
- `drug_name`;
- `approved_tier`;
- `approval_effective_date`, today as YYYY-MM-DD;
- `approval_expiration_date`, the last day the approval is in force, as YYYY-MM-DD;
- status "approved".

Status "approved" means the approval was recorded. No other outcome is defined for this tool.
